our 3rd time pilgrimage, it was really cold night, but we all can reach to the summit before the sunrise and its was a great experience for a lifetime. lots for see.. nature, tropical rainforest, waterfalls, green mountain ranges,misty peaks, it was like in a heaven.

Not for the faint hearted, physically and mentally challenging for even a seasoned hiker. But as the saying goes - no pain no gain. The pain in climbing up the steep windy path is definitely worth it! What a sight to see the sun rising from such a height. A highlight of my trip!

The steps on the way up were quite challenging and you get a bit of a sweat on, but we didn't expect it to be easy. The way down was worse as your legs turn to jelly! I agree with the review below about doing this for a fitness challenge and not for what is at the top! We were disappointed. It wasn't as cold as we thought it was going to be. I was plenty warm enough with a zip up hoodie and a thin jacket. It took us around 3 hours but we stopped off a few times. There are various tea stops and toilets. The toilet attendants charge you around 100 rupees for using their toilets. We were slightly disappointed when we got to the top as it was very crowded and everyone is crammed in behind railings so you can't see much. I would say get there early and try and sit on the steps below the railings. The best bit for us was looking out over to the left of the sunset and seeing the other route up all lit up. We took the delhousie route which didn't look as pretty from the top. It was a bit of a scramble to get down but the crowds eased quite quickly. Overall worth doing but prepare to be disappointed if you expect anything more than average!

We accidentally landed at Adams peak.. And decided to trek.. We started at 2.45AM.. And we enthusiasm we reached the top for sunrise and back to hotel by 10AM. Worth a trek.. Beautiful sunrise:) loved it.. They have small tea shops and eating place every 10 to 15 min of trek.. If you are determinate Then only trek.. My legs hurt really bad after the trek.. I couldn't walk properly for 3 days 😂..

We started our ascend at 2.30am, as suggested by the hotel we stayed at and the Lonely Planet guide. This got us up the top at 5am - 1 hour before sunrise!! That was a very cold wait for a 5 minute sunrise before the fog rolled in and we couldnt see a thing. As a fitness challenge, this was great! I just dont think its worth doing for the temple or the sunrise as the main motivation. Be prepared for the cold at the top  - take a jacket! Its concrete steps most of the time and the surrounding area is pretty dirty. No toilets, etc..,so plan your trip as well as you can.

We started the climb at 2:00 in the morning and reached the top at 4:15. Climbing up is hard, but the climb took shorter than we expected (starting at 3:00 would have been just fine). When reaching the top all warm and sweaty it was hard to imagine at first that we would be in need of all the warm clothes we brought after reading reviews here on tripadvisor. But it gets really, really cold, so pack a lot of extra layers. I froze a lot due to the fact that my shirt was kind of sweaty - so bring a dry one as well. As we climbed in high season, the path was partly lit, however you will need a flashlight. We passed several open shops on our way, but always bring water and snacks yourself in case they aren't open. The sunset, the views...amazing!! Definitely worth all the steps! We found the hardest part walking down all the steps again...and had sore legs for several days. But who cares, after such a great experience!

Long, tiring but rewarding experience. The trail is well illuminated and signed during the pilgrimage season. The path is on concrete steps up to the top, and where steep sideways handrails help to feel safe and the climb. Get to start the trail by 2.00 am and you'll enjoy the sunrise from the top. A must do experience.

Sri Lanka's highest mountain offers stunning views over the south-eastern part of the island. On a clear day you can see as far as Colombo and the airport in the north-east, and Radnapura in the east. We did a night climb with a tour guide who was helpful with pacing and pointing out what to see. We set off at 1am and reached the summit after 3.5 hours - a bit too early for the 6am sun rise. This had the advantage that we were able to visit the shrine at the summit in relative peace as it gets very crowded during the season, particularly around full moon. The hike is curious in that the path is lit in its entirety (during the season) and consists of some 6,000 steps of concrete mostly. You walk most of the time in groups with other travellers and the is quite some traffic coming your way. Lankans walk up bare feet or in flip flops, but gets pretty cold upstairs with a chilly wind and the steps are better mastered in proper closed shoes - particularly on the way down. No need to take water or snacks as there are plenty of stalls and shops along the route. Also, if you didn't bring a fleece jumper or rain jacket to SL, you can buy it there.

What a challenge! We arrived the night before our climb not really knowing fully what we were in for. Luckily we overheard some of the other tourists speak about their preparations.. We did not have a torch, but we used our phones to light the way. We did not have a guide, so we followed some other people before we got to the steps and then it's pretty straight forward. We were told it takes a minimum of 3hrs to complete, so we left at 2am in order to reach the summit by sunrise. We did it just under 2hrs which meant we had a long wait at the top, which was fun but once our body temperature dropped it was super freezing!!  Sunrise was magnificent! So happy we were able to accomplish this hike, but we couldn't walk properly for about a week after. Worth it!!

It's a long way - three hours of walking up steps. You get a rest when there's a queue. Bottlenecks form when there's an old person going slowly, or people sitting on the steps. At the top it's mayhem - queues, crowds, people waiting for dawn, nowhere decent to view the view, which direction facing to grab a viewing place?  Always a bit cold, but made worse when we were there by drizzle and wind. Cold wet barefoot mayhem. Germans with beards eating sandwiches from Tupperware boxes. Not very spiritual at all really. Weather fine further down. You could see clouds on the very top.  No need for a torch -  it's all lit. Wear comfy shoes!  Take spare socks because you have to take shoes off for the temple on the top. Your original socks will be all sweaty. No need to pack drinks / food etc there are loads of shops all the way up. Coming down is very hard on your knees - and careful not to slip on any one of those 5000 uneven steps....  So - if you go at dawn you get heaving crowds and cold summit. If you go in the day it'll be very hot. Maybe don't bother...?

The day before the hike we got to the village at the base around 2, had some food, walking around the village, showered and went to sleep at 6pm to wake for 2am to start the walk, which i'd recommend. We had a very basic hostel right at the base of the walk (green house) so it was convenient and meant no extra walking! The walk itself: I'm don't think I'm very fit and I have an extremely slow pace, but I've climbed one other mountain - Kota Kinabalu in Borneo. From the reviews I thought it would be on that level of difficultly. It's not. It's 3 hours up walking slowly. There are stairs the whole way and hand rail in steeper bits, so none of the path is really tricky. If you start at 2 you can go slow with regular breaks and not worry about missing the sunrise which for us was at 6.10am. We were going slowly and till had to rest for 45 minutes to avoid getting to the top prematurely and getting cold. You can get roti and tea on the walk up and the shop keepers there will tell you if you are too early for sunrise and to take a break! The view was lovely but what I loved was the walk down which was very pretty and we saw bee hives too which was cool. A few points of note: I had a Sri Lankan sim and had wifi all the way up. You can buy torches from the local shop before the walk but didn't see any walking sticks on sale. Don't think you really need it though. Wear layers - cold at the top, cold when you stop.

I'm unfit & 50+ . Just returned from Adam's Peak. I did the ascent at night to catch the sunrise. In the end, this wasn't possible because of the cloud cover. Nevertheless, it was a terrific experience, which I highly recommend if for no other reason than to establish the state of your coronary vessels! Some have suggested making the trek during the day. That's a fair call. In my case though, I'm glad I went at night because had i actually seen the path ahead on the ascent, I suspect I'd have given up well before the summit! And I saw lots on the way down. The experience is every bit as spectacular as others have described. The scenery, the pageantry, the tea houses, the site of the elderly on walking sticks & young adults with babes in arms climbing those exhausting steps....!!! Great fun.

My fiancé and I did the 6 hour journey from Hikkaduwa to Hatton to see the sunrise from Adams Peak and boy was it worth it! Despite staying in an awful guesthouse, Adams Peak was truly amazing. The 6851 steps get steeper as you go up and the climb tested everyone we met on the way We slept for about 4 hours before starting our climb at 01:45am. We went just the two of us as a guide is really not needed and we found our way easily. Be sure to take plenty of water, snacks (something a little more main for when you get to the the top) and your camera! There are shacks on the way up serving tea, cold drinks and various snacks should you not have time to prepare anything before hand. It is very cold when you get to the top (which took us exactly 2.5 hours from the starting point) so make sure you take a jacket, scarf, gloves, wrap, whatever you can carry.... We got to the top at 04:30am and although the sunrise was magnificent, the Stars were also truly something! The sun started shedding its light across the way at about 05:00am and eventually showed itself by 06:00am. With each minute the view from the top changed and we saw things we didn't know were there on the way up! Be sure to leave earlier and rather wait longer for the sunrise, as even out of peak season it can get too busy to get a decent spot! There were about 200 people up there with us and I would say a good 40 that arrived slightly later missed out on good viewing spots! The way down is also a challenge and your legs feel like they are trembling when you stop so it's better to just keep going! Do take some time to stop and enjoy the magnificent views of the landscape, lake and waterfalls! It was worth the 12 hours round trip, awful guesthouse experience and 4 hours sleep!

This walk was insane. The steps are very steep and the walk is quite long (about 11km each way)! We were told to leave at 1am in order to make it to the top for sunrise however we arrived about an hour prior and their was hardly any room to stand let alone sit to wait so we gave our (cash) offering and bowed to Buddha before descending. Their was huge crowds the whole journey and it is quite motivating to see little old shoeless ladies with walking sticks trekking to the top as well. The scenery in the area was beautiful and I wish we had done the climb during the day so that we could take it all in. Their was a really cool vibe on descent - kind of similar to leaving a dance party at 6am. Lots of colorful stalls, music, chanting and general happiness. Well worth the sore knees and aching calves.

Adam’s Peak or the Sri Pada is an important pilgrim site. Buddhist believes the impression on the summit is the footprint of Lord Buddha himself. Access to the Adam’s Peak is possible by 6 trails: Hatton-Nallathanni; Ratnapura-Palabaddala; Kuruwita-Erathna; Murraywatte; Mookuwatte; Malimboda.The most popular routes are the Hatton-Nallathanni & Ratnapura-Palabaddala due to the picturesque views and postcard worthy scenery that can be encountered along them. Once you reach a final node (Nallanthanni or Palabaddala or Erathna) there begins the difficult journey through the jungle on foot. Most of the pilgrims use the Hatton route as the journey can be reduced by more than five kilometers even though the slope of this route is much greater than the others. The pilgrims season to Sri Pada traditionally starts on the full moon of December and ends on the full moon of May.Accommodation on the summit of Adam’s peak is basic and you would have to bring your own food and perhaps a blanket or sleeping bag. However, whenever you decide to go, check the weather report before setting out. Rain can make for a miserable trip and it is more likely that cloud or mist will obscure the view.When the sun is just about to rise, the pilgrims and tourists rush to the eastern side to witness an amazng spectacle. The sun almost leaps over the eastern horizon drawing a perfect triangle of a shadow of the mountain spreading over the western backdrop of the mountain. As the sun keeps on rising, the shadow shifts towards the base of the mountain until it completely disappears, a grand finale to a breathtaking natural spectacle.

My family and me are Buddhist, ever since I was a child we always used to visit temples on holiday, every night, my mom told me the Buddhist stories before I sleep. I used to get bored to these all. But I don't remember and don't know why since one day I became a history of religious lover. Especially, I'm interest in religious of South Asia, for Buddhism, Hinduism...they have several thousand years histories, spectacular building, beautiful colors, and mysterious atmosphere these are all make me wanna deeper understanding. When I googled Sri Lanka travel informations, I found many websites says:According to a legend the Buddha is believed to have left the print of his left foot on Adam's Peak. As a Lankan person must to visit Adam's Peak at least once in a life time. Oh my God! I thought this is so amazing and really cool, yes! I must to visit here, so Adam's Peak be my first destination in Sri Lanka. I waked up in the early morning (half past 2 a.m.) to begin my way to climb. I need to be honest, for the first hour I thought Okay! So easy! not too cold, not too steep to climb. But in two hours, my feet were numb, asthma attack was going to happen. Many times I squatted at roadside and want to shout:"I give up!" But many Lankans people(kids, young people, elderly) they all cheer me up, told me"Keep going~ it's near." I saw many Lankans just wore flip flops even some don't wear shoes, daddies are super-hero they carried their children on their shoulder and old women wore long skirt to climbed and why they were looking so easy? I already arrived the last tea shop, a guide told me:"Relax for a while, enjoy a cup of tea. You can go with us together!" I stayed at tea shop with them, but so weird is in half hour, guide didn't round up all the members. Some of members couldn't help but ask guide:"Why are we still here? Are you sure we can see the sunrise?" Guide said:"Take easy! Believe me! It's too early, we have time!" Maybe after 15 minutes, guide told all the members ready to go. But I saw my iPhone, the time is 5:15 a.m. Oh...oh...at this moment a girl shout:"If we don't see the sunrise give our money back." Haha...Just as I thought, crowds of pilgrims already on the top at an earlier time. We couldn't  move at all. We and the top are only within 1 kilometers of each other. A girl yelled at guide, he tried to calmed her down and repeated you can't see beautiful sunrise from top, people will block your view. The dawn broke, the fight stopped, and the clouds started to part, everything around us a deep blue hue and then yellow lights atop of the buildings and ladders were sparkling... I froze, we were as if in the fairy tale wonderland. I couldn't stop taking photographs...... It was stunning made me couldn't breathe. Although I didn't see the Buddha's footprint in the top, I know Buddha always belong in our minds.

We decided to climb Adam's Peak day before the opening ceremony to avoid crowds. Unfortunately it was already pretty crowded so we didn't make it to the temple :( people were going up both sides of the way, blocking those who wanted to go down so in result they blocked the path so no one could enter for at least 40min. As we were getting to cold we decided to go back. Nevertheless it is an amazing experience. People wearing their flip flops were climbing in a cheerful mood singing and chanting. My suggestion is to take it easy on the way up, make as many stops as possible, enjoy cup of tea and to observe other people. We wanted to witness the sunrise in the temple but we would have to wait there for at least 2 hours, which was rather impossible due to cold wind and too many people.

We started the hike at 3am from Dalhousie  and, as we planned to go to the coast the next day, had the idea to go down on the Ratnapura side, to avoid approx. 8 hours of train ride. Unfortunately we planned for holiday and not longer hiking trips and so our backpacks had a weight of around 18kg, far too much for such a long way. It is around 5200 steps, 6 km and 2.5 hours on the way up and was very exhausting, even as an more of less experienced hiker. Without this much luggage, it should be way easier. On the way are plenty of shops and you can buy water, snacks and tea almost every 500m, so you don't necessarily have to carry 3 liters to the top. We had plenty of luck and when we arrived there were almost no clouds and the view was astonishing. Even if there were quite a lot of other tourists, it was a magical and special moment when the sun was visible behind the mountains for the first time. Furthermore, the triangular shadow on the other side looks amazing. Down towards Ratnapura is another 12km, more than 9000 steps and around 5 hours. We experienced all the different stages between fascination, exhaustion, resignation and dullness on the way down multiple times. The path is amazing and we were able to see monkeys and other animals but especially the last two hours are quite hard. Again, there are plenty of shops and you don't have to worry about supply also you cannot miss the way if you follow the stairs. Every 100 steps is a marker and you see the number decreasing very very slowly while following the stairs though the jungle. On the end of the path is a small village and it was absolutely no problem to get a taxi to Ratnapura (28km, 45 minutes, 1200 LKR). There is also a bus station with busses leaving frequently but we were to exhausted to go there. In the end it was totally worth it. We did not only cross a mountain to avoid 8 hours of dull train ride but also went directly through the jungle and the feeling of looking up to the highest top in the area and thinking "I have been there a few hours ago" is purely amazing. But I would highly recommend to do this only with light baggage. It was possible with two backpacks of in total 18kg but it took away a lot of the fun. Whatever you are doing, your legs are haunting you for days...

Well 1) this sounds stupid, but by sunrise they really mean sunrise - when the sun gets in the sky - but it s really nice to see the first lights, so be there about 20 min earlier than is the time locals tell you 2) dont ask anyone on the way up how far is it to the top & if you see anything as the weather is not that good... and dont trust anyone!:) half way up I heard some tourists asking local guy and he said it's too cloudy and we wont see anything - it wasnt a very good motivation... and there was also local guy running up the hill who told us we re just in the half... although we were 15min from the top and the visibility was great 3) it s not that bad, we did it in about 3h in total with waiting for each other 4) we tried both bus on the way there (2h, one change, very crowded) and taxi (45min, 2500r for 5pax) on the way back and although otherwise we only used buses and trains, this time Id vote for taxi

Well, the main aim to write this request is to make more and more people decide to go!!! It is simply amazing - when you have to make unusual and big efforts to reach the top in the night, and to see the beautiful sunrise (our`s was beyond the clouds). Nature is very beautiful, people very kind and what was amazing that such a difficult trip for tourist is everyday for those people who arranged small rest points there where one can get tea or coffee or some water. Those rest points were on the road the whole way to the top and those people carry all those snacks and drinks on their backs as no other road is there for cars.

Do not underestimate the climb - the uneven steps are relentless, the advantage of doing it at night is you can't see what lies ahead! However, the addition of numerous stalls selling hot tea and snacks since we were last there 20 years ago was welcome and the whole experience was very convivial - a real sense of camaraderie amongst the fellow masochists marching through the night!

Not recommended for the fainthearted or those who are not used to tracking but on the other hand you can always climb at your own pace and definitely no need of a guide. It's a steep 13 km up and down. Bring a lot of water with you to keep hydrated. You start in the dark and early hours and take a good torch with you. You do not realise the gem around you until sunrise or when you are coming back down. The place was crowded but we could still climb at a good pace. There is a Buddhist temple at the top from where climbers love to watch the sunrise. It gets very windy and cold, so take some extra clothing with you so that you stay comfortable up there. Very disappointed to find that the Buddha footprint was not accessible. Coming down, the scenery is awesomely picturesque with lakes and lots of waterfalls.

I went there twice. I'm a Buddhist so climbing Sri Padha and worshiping Lord Buddha's sacred foot print were in bucket list since several years. I go there by train with one of my good friend. We took train from Polgahawela and get CTB bus from Hatton to Nallathanni (Which is starting point of Nallathanni Sri Padha road). It's the shortest path to the sacred mountain. There are another two popular paths and several hidden paths as well. Small stores all the way to the top. But when you go higher on the mountain prices also goes higher and I think it's reasonable. If you are a local like me or from tropical country I advice you to bring warm cloths otherwise you will be fine. Wait till sun dawn. It's beautiful. Best time to climb mountain after 20th of March. Before that it filled with people you have to wait several minutes to climb next step :).

We did this climb at the start of the season so the trail wasn't lit but cafes were open. Head torches are a must- nearer the top you'll want both hands to help you up the steps! The steps are VERY steep so be prepared. I am moderately unfit so this climb was tough but still very doable- just be aware that coming down is almost worse than going up as your muscles are likely to be shot! We arrived at the summit for sunrise, but by the time 6.15 came around, we were enveloped in clouds, and actually couldn't see a thing- very disappointing! But after hanging around for half an hour, we did periodically get some cool misty views of the surrounding mountains. But overall the views were lacklustre because of the clouds- it's just luck how the weather is on the day but be prepared to avoid disappointment!

Would do this again in a heart beat!!! Do NOT get a "guide". Its a scam for your money. We did it fine without one. There are signs everywhere. Its "free" which actually means - donate to the monk who sits and waits for tourists to give him money. The hike is plenty hard, so bring lots of snacks and water. It gets VERY cold at the top, so bring a hat and gloves. Im serious. It gets bloody cold. Sunrise is amazing. On the way down you spot all the countless waterfalls you missed on your way up in the dark.

We left at about 4: 50 am as we thought it would be easier for our 7 and 9 year old boys. Turned out to be a great idea. We walked by ourselves the whole way and had the summit all,to ourselves when we got there about 7:30. The views were still fantastic, we saw sunrise from a good vantage point anyway and we really only missed out on the triangle shadow. In case you are wondering exactly how many steps...our boys counted all of them from the Adams peak sign over the bridge at Delhousie it was 4814 steps!!! We grabbed some bamboo for sticks which helped on the way down, but all in all the walk was not difficult , steps are in very good condition and we still had bouncing boys at the bottom. Highly recommended!

We went up in a group of 7. Naturally split into groups by speed. It was a quite a trudge at points but so worth it! At the last tea stop, the vibe is super fun and positive. Loads (almost all) foreigners hiking. The concrete temple surrounding the "footprint" is very small and annoyingly, there are metal boards blocking the footprint now. The temple grounds aren't opened until well after sunrise, which was also frustrating. Took 2 hours up at a good pace. No more than 3 for slower groups. Sunrise was stupendous! Hang around for the lush landscapes brought to life by the red light of the morning sun.

The hike is around 7km and 6000 stairs. You should leave in the night (we left around 2am) to be at the top 6am to see the sunrise from there. That was one of the most beautiful things i have seen. The hike is hard, stairs are in really bad shape, there is no toilets (only holes in the ground) and its cold and a lot of stairs. But I think its all worth it.

Climbing this is a hard task but for nature lovers it is an easy task to see the smoky mountain which is a true paradise filled with lush green forest with cool mountain streams.Adam's peak is 2243 m tall conical mountain located in central Sri lanka.The Sun rises behind from the Adam's peak indeed spectacle. As we started to climb at night we were able to see the Sun through the smoky mountain.

A challenging climb with over 5000 steps but so worth it for a stunning view, we also saw the triangular shadow in the centre of a rainbow (which was nearly circular) - stunning. Here are our best tips for staying in Delhousie and for the climb: - Delhousie is very over-priced, especially the food at hotels but there are a couple of small restuarants not attched to hotels which are much better value - Our hotel tried to make us get an overpriced rickshaw (1300 rupees) but getting the local bus is very easy and very cheap (80 rupees per person instead of over 1000 rupees for a rickshaw) in pilgramage season there are direct buses, outside of this time you can get a bus to Maskeliya (around 40 rupees) and change there for a bus or mini bus to Delhousie (again 40 rupees) - people and bus drivers are very helpful - the journey took us less than 2 hours both ways (again you will be told by hotels and rickshaw drivers that it takes 4......simply not true from our experience) Getting the bus back is also simple, ask anyone where the bus stop is in Delhousie - start early 2/2.30 am, if it is raining lightly still go as it was for us and was still beautifully clear at the top - take a change of clothes - at least a top and jumper - for the top as any mist/sweat will make you cold in the chilly wind at the top of the peak - torches are essential out of pilgramage season to see in the dark (tea shops light the way in pilgramage season) - the temple area at the top may only open at 6am out of the pilgramage season - the best place to see the triangle is on the steps leading down to the left (as you arrive up the lasy few steps, with the temple in front of you) Don't get distracted by the sunrise for too long and miss it!! It appeared around 15 mins after sunrise (before 6 am) and wasn't there long!! - some reviews mention dogs, there are stary dogs but all left us alone and posed no issue to people, more of companionship for the climb if you want them to, they just wanted to get into the bins for scraps Some reviews also mention being sore for a few days after, obviously this really depends on your level of fitness! We are reasonably fit and just felt tired in our legs the next day

We reached White house guest house near Del House in the evening, had dinner and went to sleep. We started the trek from our stay at 2:15 AM with a couple of bottles. It's advisable to carry a packet of biscuits or chocolates or fruits along with water, flash lights and some warm clothes. It's better to carry a change of shirt because you'll sweat a lot by the time you reach the top. It was a beautiful trek. Not difficult in terms of terrain, but 5,800 steps one way. The total duration will be approximately 3 hours. The sum rise begins at 5:30 AM and the sun is completely out by 6:30 AM. It's one of the most beautiful sunrises I've ever witnessed. One one side of the peak was the sun rise, on the other side was a sea of clouds. It was gorgeous! The peak also casts its shadow on the clouds. The climb down is very tiring, because your legs would be jelly by then. Highly recommended when you visit the Lanka land!

Adam's Peak is what most people associate with Sri Lanka's tea country - it is imposing and known to all and also something to do up in tea country other than eat! You needn't climb it to appreciate it, though -- the surrounding mountains are just as beautiful without the crazy crowds!

Climbing this is an exhausting task so make sure you are fit to do it. It's 5000 steps, uneven, some are really high so it's a big effort. Reaching the top is not an accomplishing moment as there are some buildings blocking the view... Of course the sunrise is beautiful to see, but I don't think it balances with the effort... You'll spend a few days recovering your legs. Do it the normal way - start climbing at 2am and go prepared because it is cold & good luck!

I was a little unprepared for what the hike up Adam's Peak had in store. Let me be clear: if you are not a seasoned hiker, then you need to do some stairs training. My fitness levels were pretty good, but it did get to a point where I thought that my legs were going to give way! All that being said, the experience was amazing. Ringing the bell in the temple, watching the incredible sunrise....it was disappointing that there were a number of concrete slab buildings up there that made it hard to rest and capture the incredible sunrise. Things to take: a torch, a warm jacket (I had a windbreaker and it was not warm enough for the top of the mountain once I had cooled down), gloves (my fingers were losing feeling) and some snacks.

My girlfriend and I visited this attraction as it was recommended as something  to do in Sri Lanka. It's a tough climb but when you get to the top you are greeted with fantastic and breathtaking views.  Well worth the effort but would advise good quality walking shoes.

We set off at 2:00 on a starlit night in November with the peak  5831 steps upwards our goal. We were joined by fellow walkers with torches along the route and were lucky that the night was clear and dry. It was pretty chilly at the top waiting for the sun to rise so warm clothes are a must, but it was well worth the trek, the views were simply stunning. It was a surreal, beautiful and tiring experience shared with friends met along the way that we'll never forget.

Quite the climb, and since you want to catch a sunrise it is advised to start walking around 2 AM as it is said to take about 4 hours. I was too stubborn and thought it wasn't that cold. It was not. Below. Once we got up there I regretted not taking a vest/jacket with me. Stupid stubborn tourist. On top of that, we did not walk it in 4, but in 2,5 hours. Meaning we were stuck for about 1,5 hours on top of Adam's peak waiting on sunrise. Definitely worth the wait though! There are places you can get a cup of coffee or tea to warm up. Might visit again this year. The 'footprint' on top in the 'temple' I completely missed though. Not too impressive.

We started our climbing at 2 o'clock in the morning so that we can enjoy the sun rise from adam peak. you should not spend money on hiring guide since you will find a lot of people from different nations on your way to climb. it took around 3 hours for us to reach to the top. It was so colt at the peak, so you should bring warm cloths with you. Climbing is never easy. However, the view you will get after climbing is worthy.

3 of us aged 26 were the first to set off at 2.30am, we got to the top at 5am, we waited an hour for sunrise and it was cold up there. There were about 100-150 people at the top for sunrise. I would recommend finding a stick to help you climb the stairs, and a big bottle of water, ooh and a spare t-shirt to change into at the top. Would highly recommend doing this, a must!
It is must visit place. As it is out of season till December, and then it will be till May, we didnot make the climb

I have done the hike first week of November and we were very lucky with the weather as there was no rain. We started to walk at 3 am and it took us 3.5 hours from the guest house, which was more than half hour away from the mountain gate. The hike was extremely difficult, specially the last steepest part. The positive thing was that there were almost no tourists (only like 25 pax on the top), as this was still low season, and I cannot imagine doing this with lot of people around, since road is quite narrow in last parts, hard to take over. The road was not litten, so it is good to have the headlight. I got beaten by leach, which I didn't feel at all, just found a bloody stain on my sock. It is good to take some extra clothes in backpack as my T-shirt was completely wet from sweat. I had just jacket, but it would be better to change to something dry. The top was also a little dissapointment as I has expecting some magnificent temple,  but there is not much to see. On the other hand the view from top is amazing, something you can never forget. The way down was quite quick, less than 2 hours, but also not easy because the muscles on my legs we in pain. The following 2 days I couldn't even step from my bed, it was such a terrible muscle sore.

I went to Adam's peak "out of the season", when they say you can rarely see something, but it was wonderful. We have started at 2:30AM, and we have arrived to the top around 5:30AM, We have seen the wonderful sunrise, and after around 2 hours it became cloudy. The same experience have had many people I have met in these days (few days before or after) so don't trust the weather forecast and don't  give up just because of the bad weather in the afternoon - in the morning it can still be nice... at least these few hours to make you see the sunrise and come down safely. I was staying at White house guesthouse, which is really a great place with great stuff, they perfectly complement the wonderful experience of Adam's peak!!!

We climbed the steps in the afternoon from the Hatton trail. It was a really tough climb so be prepared. When we were nearly at the top, another couple were coming back down in quite a rush. We asked if they enjoyed it and they said that they didn't get to see anything because there were lots of wild dogs and pigs at the top and it was a really scary experience. We decided not to go up and take the risk of being attacked or bitten. We would advise anyone making the trek at this time of year to be really careful as we had such a stressful experience. It was really disappointing as we had climbed for hours to see the footprint and enjoy the view. Descending the steps was really scary as we could hear the wild dogs and monkeys calling out nearby. There was no mention of dogs or pigs in any guides so thought we should mention it.

A must see and a great hike if you are fit to climb. You should climb this during the season which is from December Poya Day to May Wesak Poya. The climb should be in the evening in order to get to the top to witness the sun rise which is best feature of this attraction. Even if you do decide to climb this during the off season, its still doable during day time since there wont be power in the nights and with very less provisions on the way up during the off season.

My boyfriend and I started walking from our hotel/guest house at 3 am to be sure we would make it to the top before sunrise which started at 5:30. We read on TripAdvisor and heard from several locals that it would take 2,5 - 3 hours to reach the top, we made it in 1,5 hours. We are in fairly good shape I would say, but the fact that we are very competitive also helped us a lot, hehe. We made it to the top approximately 1 hour before the sunrise started and it was already packed with people. Remember to bring WARM clothes! It gets cold at the top because of the wind and because you've just completed a crazy workout consisting of over 5000 steps. The sunrise was spectacular so remember to bring your camera! I was honestly a little disappointed because I expected the top of the mountain to be more "serene", but the top is covered with buildings (including one temple) and the day we were there it smelt pretty bad. All the buildings make it kind of hard to get a good picture and good view. Though I would say the hike is well worth it because of the workout and sunrise, I was a bit disappointed when I made it to the top (but VERY relieved and very exhausted).

The really steep steps up to the top are tough- I am done the three peak challenge and am fairly young (26years old) and thought this would be a walk in the park. I was wrong. I was sweating buckets on the ascent which took 2hrs 20mins from the hostel. Do take warm clothing as you are likely to be damp from the climb and need i would say two extra layers once you arrive at the top. Time it right and you should have only a bit of time to wait for sunrise. The walk down took longer than the ascent so keep that in mind. Also if you see locals carrying white heavy sacks up the mountain on your way down they are carrying them for a construction project 2/3 of the way up. They get paid 30r/kg and they carry between 25-40kg. Sobering thought right?

Well worth the hike up for the views and to snap some great photos. The peak didn't open until 6am so take you're time walking there or sleep in those extra minutes. Takes approx 2.5 for moderately fit people

It was one of the best experiences of our Sri Lanka trip. Weather was great even off season and we have seen the sunrise. There were just several groups of people with us, so the climb was pretty smooth. My calves were still sore about 3 days after climb..

Well, well, You're not a true Sri Lankan if you haven't been here yet :p Great hiking experience. And I DO NOT recommend the Hatton route with many steps which is shorter and less time consuming. But Ratnapura route is god damn awesome. Which take more time and longer. Nearly 16km. Trust me, you'll love the Ratnapura route!
It a Religious Place in Sri Lanka. Must start at night then you can see beautiful sunrise in the morning.

I completely underestimated how hard his would be. My god it killed my legs!!  It took us about 3 hours to get up and 2 hours to get down, maybe less because we sat at the top for a good half hour. We sadly went when it was offseason so all the stalls and temples were closed which was a shame but we still climbed it and had a great day! A lot of people climb this at 3am so that they reach the top but sunrise but we actually climbed this at around 11am so if you choose to do that take LOTS of water and sun cream!! This is a must do thing if you are going to Sri Lanka! Hatton itself is also such a beautiful place so the road trip to Adams peak was breathtaking! I have posted some pictures of Hatton also to let you see.

We started our hike at 2.30. It's a dificult climb, especially the last 20 minutes. After 2,5 hours we reached the top. We are not advanced mountain climbers, but quite sporty, I can say. Make sure to bring warm clothes to wear at the top. During the climb, thin pants and a shirt is enough. Sneakers or trekking shoes are good to wear.

We didn't have a view from the top as it was cloudy and it was also lashing rain when we did the walk BUT every member of our group of 7 would recommend doing this. It takes about 3hrs up and 2hrs or so down but where it's not cloudy the view is fab and you feel like you've achieved something (though we had very stiff legs for a couple of days after!). We started the climb at 2.30am and were at the peak in time for sunrise (though we didn't see a proper sunrise due to the clouds). Bring waterproofs, water and a snack for the top!

We went up Adams Peak in off season (Season is from December to May). Other tourists and even locals dissuaded us from going up there because of the weather. We heard that the last weeks always had been cloudy, rainy and misty and that you could not enjoy the breathtaking view. But we did it anyway. I am a sports student and my friend was quite fit as well so we managed the stairs in 2:45 hours, with many water brakes and some star gazing. We started at 2:30 am and arrived just in time to watch the sunrise. It was one of the best experiences of my life. Unforgettable! If you are uncertain whether to go or not in off season ... JUST DO IT!   We were lucky but even if the weather is not as good its an experience you will never forget. Take lots of water, food, warm clothes (not for the way up but up there it going to be freezing cold) and a torch (you can buy one for 100 rupiah). Before you go up a monk blesses you and ties a little string around your wrist. When you arrive at the top you meet people from all over the world. They offered hot tea. We snuggled us inside our blanket, drank the tea and watched the sun rise. It was so beautiful I still get emotional thinking about it. At 6 o´clock they open up a little stairway from which you have a better view across the roofs (I don't understand the reason why people built these houses they block the view in every direction). Afterwards they opened the temple. Have a look around but keep in mind that you have to take off your shoes (cold feet) and be quiet. You can ring the bell, take a picture of the shadow of the peak in the clouds behind it and talk to locals. On the way down you get one nature blast after another. All the beauty you couldn´t see on the way up opens up in front of you when heading down. If you can manage it try to run down the stairs. It its way easier. But you will have stiff muscles for the next few days anyway. A monk blessed us again with another wrist band and a yellow dot on our foreheads. We greeted tea-pluckers that went to work and washed our faces in the fresh creek. All in all an amazing experience I can only recommend to any nature lover that is willing to go above and beyond.

Grab a few hours sleep so you are rested and ready for the climb, it may be steps but it gets tougher the higher you get. On your ascent take a few moments to turn off your torch and enjoy the night sky, very very little pollution so the starscape is very clear. We were lucky enough to see shooting stars. On reaching the top there is a real sense of camaraderie with fellow climbers and you soon forget how exhausting the climb was. There are a couple of chaps selling tea, you definitely need that to warm you up. The sunrise is so beautiful and the clouds that fill the valleys are like big marshmallows. We climbed in September along with maybe 50-100 others who chose to do it out of season and I would say take a chance and do it. I doubt it would feel as special during pilgrim season when the space is packed. Top tips. Turn off your torch. Pack layers. Put down your camera and take in the moment.

YES! Do it! Even offseason it was still one of the highlights of our trip. It was hard even though we were a group of fit people - did it in 2 hours 15 mins. The feeling of conquering a mountain is incredible and you get to walk through a clouds and then above them - literally. Make sure you wait until they open the temple so you can ring the bell - I know it sounds silly but it feels like such an achievement haha. We saw older and old couples making it to the top, we also encountered less fit people turning back. Just do it anyway, it will be hard but it will also be something you will remember for the rest of your life. Also, I carried a big thermos of tea with me and I hated it every bit of the way up but boy was it worth it once we got up. Even though they do make tea for you there haha - but in much smaller quantities than I needed at the moment. Bring something warm with you and eventually a spare t-shirt so you can change the one you made wet with your blood, sweat and tears. Mainly sweat and tears haha. Also, what everybody else fails to mention are the leeches. It was quite rainy when we were there and there were leeches EVERYWHERE. I managed to stay away from them by tucking my pants into the socks and my blouse into my pants and spraying all possible entry points (socks, shoes, collar, waist) with 50% DEET.

We were off season so here's a few tips: 1) it's foggy up on the top so you won't really get to see the sunrise- therefore no need to wake up at 3 AM... you can wake up at 6AM and climb in day light- we did it and got the same view (fog) that the other groups (who woke up early and climbed while it was raining). 2) you don't need a guide- you are climbing stares. at the beginning you can ask the locals where Adam's peak is. 3) Although you don't actually get to see any view on top, the climb is wirth it because: a) it's challenging and you feel really good after completing it. b) the views along the way are beautiful. c) even if it's raining- get some rain coats and enjoy the rainy weather :-).

We are group of 7 ppl went to adam's peak on Sep 26th(off season). Basically no one will say the exact kms and local people around there says it's a belief not to say. When we started walking it was around 9am. Started our trek with lots of biscuits. To our surprise there were lots of shops but all was closed as it was a off season, when we crossed first small bridge rain started and mist covered the entire place. These shops acted as our shelters :-) Almost 45 mins we couldn't trek as rain started heavily and steps became wet. Once we crossed the second bridge all the steps were steep and it became harder for us to cross 30 to 50 steps at one stretch. Rain started again and we started walking in rain in the steep steps which even made our journey very tough. People who came down said the whole place covered with mist and the couldn't see any. Note down the points before trekking adam's peak: 1. Don't trek when it is raining(you can't predict the weather out there) 2. Make up your mind for some hard stuff trekking with the steep steps ahead 3. Don't ask how much time or kms to anyone(it discourages your effort) 4. Sunrise should be awesome but don't try this in rainy season as mist would cover the entire place 5. Last but not least try to reach the top Breathe taking views will vanish all your pain :-)

The real way to do it is leave at 2 or 3am from a hotel and then walk up. For us it was 23000steps to go up and down the stares, so don't underestimate this. The walk is then in the beginning a bit boring as yiu cannot see anything, but then when light begins to shine, it absolutely amazing!

Me and my wife yesterday visited Adam's Peak. It was extremely challenging and tough, but of course doable. You need to carry lots of water and some snacks too. Taking frequent rests would help you regain strength. We started climbing around 6am and arrived at the summit by 9:15am. Since it's off season they don't show the footprint but it's really a gorgeous experience. The spectacular views, water falls, clouds, mist, all make this an AMAZING JOURNEY!

My brother managed to do it all, we have just climbed the 2 km of it. Very beautiful nature, but 7 km of climbing was too much for the most of us. Unfortunately all little romantic shops on the way were closed and my brother said, next day, that the gate to the temples on top was also close. Pity

Located approximately 154 km from Colombo and may take up to 5-6 hours one way due to narrow road and partly poor condition of the road. Prime means to access is taxi or mini bus/van for more than 5 passengers. Adventure includes climbing, seeing unique sunrise and seeing foot print of Bhudda / Adam in a temple at top. Climbing is possible throughout the year. For footprint  visit between December to July ie tourism season (otherwise temple is closed) etc. For sunrise, climb such that you are at the top before sun rise. For fit climbing time upto 2.5 hours, for medium upto 4 hours and others should not attempt. Torch is must for night climbing. Rain coat is optional if if you are ready to get wet. Guide not recommended. Approximately, as told by guide, 5660 steps. Really tough but not impossible. Take along water and cookies as per your taste. Ideally, reach base by evening, have dinner, take rest and start off by after mid night. You will be free before mid day. A number of hotels available and can be booked through web.Test yourself.

Adam's Peak (also Sri Pada; Sinhalese Samanalakanda - සමනළ කන්ද "butterfly mountain", and also ශ්‍රී පාදය "Sri Paadaya"; Tamil Sivanolipatha Malai - சிவனொளி பாதமலை), is a 2,243 m (7,359 ft) tall conical mountain and a Buddhist pilgrimage site located in central Sri Lanka. It is well known for the Sri Pada, i.e., "sacred footprint", a 1.8 m (5 ft 11 in) rock formation near the summit, which in Buddhist tradition is held to be the footprint of the Buddha, in Hindu tradition that of Shiva and in Islamic and Christian tradition that of Adam, or that of St. Thomas.[1] In Islamic tradition it is the site where Adam fell to earth and where his footprint can be found.[2] Geography

Left at 2:30am from our hotel in the village Nallathanniya. We've made it to the top in 2hrs and 15min, but are a young couple. The length for the hike will be 2-2,5hrs for well trained and 2,5-3hrs for average walkers. It's an exhausting and long trip, we were there at low season so walked most of the time allone in total darkness. You should definitely bring a flashlight, warm clothes (10-15 degrees) and the most important thing: a dry shirt for when you are at the top! The effort is totally worth it! The view during sunrise is stunning as well are the panoramic views when you hit the stairs downwards the valley.

Well there are three access routes to the summit all people use the easy route which takes about 3-4 hours of hiking but i have done the hiking through all three routes but the most beautiful routes are the two routes which takes one day to climb and one day to get down

Always been a big fan of scaling a mountain for a nice sunrise but unfortunately the morning I went up the cloud came in and spoiled the view. Still was able to have a nice view of the valley but the cloud cover was low enough to block out the horizon and unable to see the sun rise. I climb in May which is the fringe time of the season so it can go either way for the views. April and before hand is a much better time to go. The climb itself is easy to intermediate, I think from memory there are roughly 5000 steps to the top so some level of fitness is require, but in saying that I climbed with a friend who did the trek in flip-flops without issue so based on that it's not that bad. For accommodation on a budget, stay at the Green House in Dalhousie. Cheap rooms and they do a good dinner. The guesthouse is right at the beginning the trail leading up to the mountain steps.

An amazing place, truly breath taking. That View aswell! its so worth the climb. as its a local pilgrimage there are soooooooo many people you really cannot get yourself ready for how busy it will be! but dont be put off it will be one of the best days you have in sri lanka its truely beautiful x a lovely thing also is it has a second name, Butterfly mountain.. its gained this name because thousands of butterflys migrate to adams peak every year to mate and die. beautiful place.

We did the climb from Nallathaniya in August 2015. Was raining heavily during the afternoon, but woke up ap 1.45am with bright sky! We started the climb at 2.30am and arrived at the top after 2h and 15min. Climb was challenging at time, particularly the last part, but by far the descent is a lot more tiring on the legs. Temple was closed but a monk was awake and started selling cups of hot tea for 70LKR to warm you up. It felt hot up until the last 2 km, after that I started wearing more clothes. At the top it was very cold. Good job we brought plane blankets and had a change for the soaking wet t-shirt. Sunrise was AMAZING! Definitely worth the climb! Since it was low season, we encountered less than 100 people on the top and had to climb in the dark. We used our phones' lantern tool and it was more than enough.

Hard to find the entrance in low season. Cross the bridge after the big buddha, turn left and then right. There you will see the first sign. No need for an expensive guide. Bring your headlight, especially in low season because some lights don't work, and it gets difficult to see the steps. Bring warm clothing for the top. It is very windy and chilly. In off season only one shop is open. This is at the beginning of the tracks. Make sure to leave the start with enough water and powerfood. The whole ride to the top should be qualified as hard. It took us, without breaks, 105 minutes. With over 5000 steps your legs and especially calves will be put to the test. We were sore for 3-4 days. If you're lucky you will be rewarded with a beautiful view on top of the mountain. Make sure to stop at the first building. There is a small plateau on your left. Here you will have the best view (including the valley). You won't see the valley if you stand on the big plateau (tribune at the gate of the temple). At the other side of the mountain you can see it's shade in the clouds if you're lucky. Don't wait too long for the way back. Temperature will rise quickly and it will still be around 2-3 hours to get down.
Always keep it for the last day like I did. The sheer exhaustion will not allow you any further  adventure or movement.

We climbed up to the top of Adams Peak with my two children (14 and 17 years old). The weather was couldy so we could not enjoy the landscape. However, this was a great experience. Do not take a guide, this absolutly not necessary. Save this money to help local people for exemple.

Climb to Adam's Peak is very demanding. Up leads about 5,500 stairs that are quite steep. It is advisable to go around 2 o'clock in the morning to see the sunrise. Hike takes about 3,5 hours. At the top you can get a warm tea. We visited Adams Peak in September and unfortunately we were not lucky with the weather. At the top we saw only fog, it was very windy and it was really cold. On the way down it started to rain a bit. It is not a high season in September, so there were not so much people. The path was not illuminated, so it is advisable to take some light. Nature is truly breathtaking there. Everything is beautifully green, there are high hills and waterfalls, monkeys running around everywhere. Tea plantations are all around. On my opinion, it is worth to visit this place at any time of year. It's an unforgettable experience, and after a hike you will be very proud of yourself :)

3 of us climbed Adams peak at 2:30am. We made it to the summit at 5:30am. Unfortunately,  the Sun never got through the clouds and we descended an hour later.  There is a temple there which only opens between December and May. The climb down is beautiful!

Really recommend this climbing adventure, worth every step, every drop of sweat and every heartbeat!  Keep hydrated, make sure you've got some dry clothes to change into when you get on the top-as it might be a bit chilly in the morning. Local "eateries" nearby might be a good choice for dinner before you embark your climb. Don't hesitate to eat with the locals-suits to any wallet and their cuisine is delicious!

The 7km upward climb was very difficult, becoming worse (inevitably) the higher we got. 5500 steps up didn't sound much to me... Boy did I underestimate it! My fiancé couldn't make the top due to asthma and a severe case of it being 530am and we'd been hiking since 3am. I went on my own but only out of sheer stubbornness.. It was exceptionally difficult and I was climbing with my hands and knees by the end. The sunrise was absolutely gorgeous, stunning over mountainous terrain with a lake in view. I didn't quite get to the top by sunrise but I'm actual glad I didn't as when I got to the temple at the top there were too many clouds and we couldn't see anything anyway! I naively hadn't looked it up and didn't even know there was a temple so was very glad I had a jumper in my bag to cover my shoulders or I wouldn't have been allowed in anyway. You can ring the bell up the top and it's a nice atmosphere. I'm so glad I did it - the most gruelling test I've put myself through but I wouldn't do it again.. The way down is 100% worse than the way up as your legs are all wibbly and it took an hour longer. Also I got burnt on the way down despite it being 9am (damn my pale English skin) so if you're prone to burning, take some cream as it's not a quick run back down. Also. Water. Take lots of it.

A nice long climb. To catch a view of Adam's Peak shadow on the clouds, one needs to be at the top before sunrise. Otherwise take a leisurely walk. Beware of raining season when there are leeches in the streams and nearby tea plants.

Viev from the top is worth effort, which will be climbing 7 km upstairs at night...but the sunset is amazing so prepeare for unforgettable moments... it xan be crowded on the very pic so consider watching the sunrise from a few steps below the top! Same viev, less crowded!

As we have limited time and wanted to squeeze in this trip to Adam's Peak, we certainly didn't think that it's worthwhile to be honest.  Adam's Peak was out first stop when we touched down to in Sri Lanka. We hired a private cab which cost about $100 one way and it took slightly more than 2 hours to get there as opposed to taking the train which is cheaper but takes about 5 hours or so. With limited time, we slept in a little before we got up and started our hike up about 3am+.  Hike was pretty challenging but definitely doable. However, another point to note was that from most of the TA reviews that we've read, most shared that it will be cold up there but trust me it wasn't. We're from Malaysia and there wasn't a need for winter clothing. Probably just a windbreaker will do (just in case it rains). Other than the chants and procession at the top, there weren't anything much. If it rains or gets foggy at the top, you can't catch the sunrise. Nonetheless, with the history behind it and if you aren't in a hectic trip, do visit Adam's Peak.  I suppose the train ride would be more scenic than the private cab.
We started early morning 2AM to scale the peak. Its around 7500 feet above sea level. Amazing experience.

We have climbed the summit of addams peak and dronk one of the best and amazing black tea of the world. The walking started at 2.00 am in the morning and finished nearly 5.00 am. It was wet but very enjoyable moment. Especially walking under misty but peaceful places. You should definitely visit adams peak. It is rlght adress ..

We recently did the climb on July 19th. We started at 2:30am, and got to the top at about 5:15am. We took our time on the way up, and are of average fitness. I would recommend leaving around 3am, otherwise you will be waiting at the top in the freezing cold for too long. We climbed in the wet season, and was met with a white cloud of fog at the top. It was still an enjoyable journey, and worth a shot at seeing the sunrise. There were no stalls open on the way up, and very dark. Bring all the food and water you need. Bring lights, and lots of warm clothing for when you reach the top. The wind will cut right through you. We climbed in t-shirts on the way up, and then had to put on about 5 layers to stay warm. Bring rain gear all year round. The path is clear and paved, so you won't get lost. Stay at Slightly Chilled Guesthouse, they have great food, and brekkie buffet for when you get down. At the top they make you take off your shoes to walk around, so be prepared to have freezing cold feet. Our legs were sore for about 5 days afterwards, any stair was painful for days. Have fun!

Climbed Sri Pada/Adams Peaks during the off season (July 2015) and hubby and I found it exhilarating even though the weather conditions were bleak. In the days leading up to the day of our climb, it had been raining and the cloud cover had been low, so we opted to start at 6am, rather than the usual 2am-ish time during the high season. We took it easy due to the wet/windy conditions and reached the mist covered peak in around 3ish hours and 2ish to come down. While there are steps to the top, some are quite steep in places and a bit slippery given the conditions. There are, however, handrails in some sections. Temple - we were aware that during the low season it was likely to be closed, but a number of people coming down didn't seem to know this and advised us the gate was locked. Shoes & clothing - we encountered some decent rain and in certain parts of the climb it was exposed, so the chilly wind whistled across our path. We were glad we wore our lightweight hiking shoes, wore caps and merino tops and carried raincoats. We were surprised to see people just starting their climb wearing flip/flops and no raincoats. Shops - as it was the low season, we found there were only 2 stores open along the way for drinks & snacks, but we were prepared and had packed water, snacks and a sandwich in our day packs. Toilets - there are a couple on the track and one set were definitely clean (take your own paper and hand sanitizer).

Sri Pada (Adam Peak) have an amazing energy. I climbed middle of July 2015. I went not to see the sunrise rather to feel the footprint energy. Truly the energy is there also an amazing view. It took me 2 hours 15 minutes. The climb is hard. Some waterproof jacket is needed (in case it rains), a bottle of drinking water, comfortable sport shoes and extra t-shirt. No rain during that evening. Some clouds at the top coming and going but nothing serious. Its is possible to climb at anytime. All the stores were closed. It was even better. Just few people. a very nice climbing alone. Amazing experience.
You will Enjoy for sure. It was a impossible for me climb and thanks heaps to Mr.Sarath who took me up and trained me to climb up and down comfortably to the Peak.

First of all: ask yourself in which month you will visit Sri Lanka, then decide if you want to visit Adam's Peak. In December and January the weather conditions are the best and you will have the biggest change the Peak will not be in the clouds (so you can enjoy the views!). Until March the weather can be good, just watch the weather forecasts the week before you are planning to go. The other months.. it is often rainy and most of the time the peak sits in the clouds. Also, the temple at the top will be closed. In these months, consider why you want to climb. Climbing Adam's Peak is a challenge! If you are reasonable fit you will be able to climb from Nallathnniya to the top in 2,5 to 3 hours. But if you have bad knees or are otherwise not fit, don't underestimate climbing more than 5,000 slippery steps! In December with full moon lots and lots of pilgrims climb the Peak. Everywhere there are tea houses open and the route is lit by thousands of lights. This must be a real experience, but expect it to be crowded and if more than 6,000 people climb, you might not be able to reach the summit because it will be full of people.
Identified by Buddhists as the Buddha's footprint, by Hindus as that of Shiva, and by Muslims as Adam's

This was a really great experience! However it was really exhausting! If you are not in good physical shape...don't do it. You do not need to be an Olympic athlete, but should be capable to walk on over 5000 unevenly shaped steps...high that can be between 3 cm and 50 cm.

Climbed by day during wet season.  Started in nice weather but it steadily deteriorated.  We took about 3 hours up and 2 back down and realised we were not as fit as we thought!  Everything hurt for a few days afterwards.  We were persuaded by our driver to hire a guide (Rs3,000) but really not worth it and no need. Worth doing even in wet season; in dry season, would be stunning.

It's a decent trek; however, the steps are uneven that make the trek tough. We visited the place during our honeymoon and limped for 3 days after that :-D. The best part was that the weather was great and if you get a good company then you don't exactly feel tired. We trekked the peak in Dec 2013, a couple of days before the "season", so it was less crowded but locals had started setting up their shops, which worked in our favor as we had some refreshments on our way. My only advice is that go only if you have some spare day offs to cool off after you are done with the trek.

I went during off peak - so it was quite quiet.  The climb itself is not difficult, just a lot of steps up to the top and not much of a scenery as you start at around 2am in the morning.  THe climb up takes about 3H and once up there, you will have to brave the cold weather to wait for the sunrise.  There isn't much of a view from up there.  Going down is easy.  You can easily do this on your own especially during peak season. During offpeak, I hired a guide which was helpful as I was alone and the hike up took place in the dark.
Great hike, even in off-peak season, and even though you might not see a thing from the top!

We climbed off-season but couldn't make it to see the sunrise. It took us around 6hours all in all. This is a rather hard climb so make sure you bring some water and some snacks. I personally found the descent harder... Even though it was a foggy/rainy day we did enjoy it (a glimpse of the view)

i climbed adam's peak in mid-june and the weather was pretty bad. there was no sunrise or any views and the temple was locked. i didn't even get a glimpse of the mountain. so my advice is that if you are after the views and you happen to be there during the rainy season, don't climb it. but if you're already there and you like the challenge of climbing 5000+ steps in the dark, go ahead. it's worth it. since i can't comment about how beautiful it is, i'll just give some tips. 1. do bring a good torch/flashlight. although the temples and some stalls have lights, it's dark most of the time. 2. there is a bus that goes straight from hatton to dalhoussie even in the off-season. but they are less frequent. just change bus in maskeliya. the trip takes about 2.5 hours. 3. if you want to hire a tuktuk from hatton to dalhoussie v.v., the going rate is 1200LKR. the trip takes an hour. 4. there will be at least one open stall selling tea/water/biscuits even during the off-season. even if it is raining. 5. it's okay to start climbing at 2.30am. i took a lot of stops but still got to the top in less than 3 hours. 6. rooms are pretty cheap during the off-season. you can get a double room with private bath for 800LKR.

Amazing experience! I would do it again any time. The climb wasn't that hard as I imagined and the view was incredible and breathtaking (sunrise). Totally worth it! It took us about 3 hours to climb up and ~2h to descend.

Adam's peak is situated at Ratnapura district and can reach wither from Rathnapura or Hatton. We've visited drom Rathnapura side starting to climb Adam's Peak from Nallathanni area. Total hike is approximately 6kms long but takes around 5-6 hours to reach the top. Adam's peak is a  pilgrimage symbol of buddhists, where most locals climbs it during the season from December to May. Best time to climb the mountain us atarting from night, targeting to reach the top by early morning. Seenories are amazing from the top of the mountain when the sun is rising....

To climb around 5,500 stairs is a very tough challenge. Well to get down after the climb is yet a more bitter one. Well I was part of a TV program and we had the challenge to climb Adam's peak with the back packs and sleeping bags. We started the trip at around 2am. We were in 10 and managed to get to the top in 4 hours. We had seen the sunrise and it was something you do not see everyday...well from that height! I also enjoyed the way down as you can see the flora and fauna. getting down took us around 6 hours. BUT I think without any extra weights one could reach the top in 2.5 hours non-stop. Getting down requires more attention as an error may be fatal.

Average as I didn't manage to complete it. I can't speak for those who did it during the on season. It rains a lot at nights during the off season and the rain can get very heavy, making the steps slippery and the temperature very very cold. I turned back halfway with a group of people as it was too cold and rainy to continue. However I was in a tee shirt and shorts. If you'd like to tackle it during the off-season, I'd suggest bringing a good rain coat, a water proof bag, a,change of clothes for when you reach the top and a sweater in case it gets too cold. Definitely doable, but I just wasn't in the right attire for it.

I left at 2:15am to leave enough time for sunrise at Adams peak. The climb is tough, about 5500 stairs! I was lucky enough to have a clear spectacular sunrise in the off season. If the weather is overcast/misty I wouldn't bother as the main reason for the walk is the view. The temple in the off season leaves a lot to be desired. (I didn't actually go in)

We climbed in off season on an overcast, damp day, nonetheless the climb was quite rewarding! We climbed the 5000 plus steps in around 2hrs 20minutes, starting at 6am. The first hour or so of the climb is quite easy going with the steps only getting quite steep toward the last half hour. With concrete stairs the whole way it is a very safe and easy ascent and descent. Only requires a bit of fitness to make it!  Although we were unable to get a view from the top due to cloud cover, it was still an extremely beautiful climb.

We decided to hike up Adam's peak to see the Sunrise. Left at 2am. Took us 2h and 48min so we were up there quite early and had to wait for an hour for the sun to rise. It gets quite cold and windy on top so would recommend coat and socks ( you have to take your shoes off up there). We hiked during bank holiday so the place  was very busy. Watch for your backpacks! Otherwise, it was stunning. Beautiful views, great experience and something I would def do again , it's def worth it!!!!

Claim Adams Peak was supposed to be highlight of our trip. I started claiming @ 2:30am. Toke with me as less as possible. It wasn’t season  so only 1 shop was open on the way to top and no lights were on. So make sure you have torch with you. Middle of the way started to rain so were wet top to bottom when reached top @5 am. It was extremely cold and windy there.  Because of the rain we couldn’t see sunrise and for whatever reason Temple was closed.  With big disappointment started coming down. Tip - dont plan anything  for next couple of days( beach only) as you might have some walking difficulties :)

I came 1 week after the pilgrimage season, so the ENTIRE town and trek was pitch-dark. It was like a ghost-town with abandoned stalls! So if you're doing the climb during this period (mid-may to dec), please bring a torch, water, jacket and some food. After reading the reviews by travellers who came during the pilgrimage season, it's really a total opposite atmosphere! (Let me also add this: despite what ALL tuk-tuk drivers tell you, there ARE frequent buses from Hatton to Dalhousie during off-season. I was convinced to take a Rs1300 tuk-tuk from hatton station, but the next morning, I took a Rs70 DIRECT bus back from Dalhousie. I found out, because i saw many buses, and I asked one of the drivers for the bus frequency. I also saw a policeman near the start of the trek, and he also confirmed there are Direct buses between Dalhousie and Hatton. Alternatively, you may transfer very easily at Maskeliya town, which is halfway between Hatton and Dalhousie. Just ask around and save 20 times the money, for about the same journey time! And it's quite an experience to ride with the locals!) Back to the trek, it probably would also have been a great experience during the off-peak season, because the lack of lights and people and sounds, made it a pretty peaceful climb. I reckon if the weather is good, you can see stars easily without the light pollution. I started my trek solo, and only caught up with 2-4 other travellers after 20 minutes. (I was thankful though, because it really was unnerving to be alone in the darkness!) I started at 2:15am, and reached the peak at 5am. It was drizzling throughout the trek, and yes - during such foul weather, you see NOTHING at the top. It was all misty and there're zero views and it was cold! But still, since you're there, it doesn't make sense not to climb it right, because at least you can still talk about conquering another mountain. During off-season, the temple gates are locked up. So you don't get to enter the temple; don't get to see the footprint; don't get to sound the bell like pilgrims. What you see, is really just a locked gate at the top of the flight of stairs. That's all. But from pictures that I saw, a beautiful sunrise would await you. Unless it's foul weather like mine.. :(

One of the best hikes I have had. Ideal to start the hikes early morning before sunrise, and we started around 2 am. Usually people go there in the early morning to start the climb straight away, but we went in an evening and stayed at one of the rest houses at the base. There were porters to take our bags from the car park to the house. After dinner and a nice nap we started climbing early morning and was able to stay and worship the sri pada as well. Then we were back at the rest house by 10 am. Surprising we didn't even feel a bit tired.One of the best memories was to see the sun rise in early morning , called "Irasewaya". Not to miss "Seeths gangula and Indikatupana . Mostly the worshipping or the trailing period is 6 months starting from December full moon day to May. This is surely a grand experience for anyone who is looking  for an amazing adventure. Warm clothes are advised to be taken due to the cold breeze at the peek.  Hoping to go again soon.

Adam's peak is a must do activity in Sri Lanka if you can fit with your itinerary.if you are with kids or if you are older person then you may stay away going there as it more suitable for people who climbs and adventure type experiences. Best time to climb adam's peak is December to may as you will find many facilities available during this time as it is the season for adam's peak . However if you like your own undisturbed climbing then go on off season but at least go with 1friend.

Started our ascent at 02:00 and arrived to top at 05:45... I do not know is it fast or slow result, doesn't matter! Bottom of line is - at the end this is like "maya bay" at PhiPhi = you expect something special, but its ruined by tourists... But and once again but - this is physical and mental challenge you must try to get know yourself better! Pack good hydration equipment headlight and start you journey... good luck!
You can easily climb Adam's peak in less than 3 hours. You'll need way more time if you stop at every shop you encounter (there is a lot of shops on the way…)

We had such a great guide from Ceylon Tea Trails - who was on his 60th climb for this year.  With his encouragement we made it to the top and to the temple.  He then took us down to his favorite spot to watch the sunrise.  It was less crowded and a perfect spot to have a little breakfast before heading back down.  This was such a great experience and definitely a highlight of our trip to the Ceylon Tea Trails.  We did this at the end of March and needed warm clothing as we got closer to the top - so layering is best.  Doing this climb in the dark hours of the morning means that the rest of the day could be a bit of a write off in that you end up returning around 9am, eat breakfast and then feel like sleeping the rest of the day.  Just something to keep in mind if you have other activities planned in a short stay.

Do yourself a favour whilst in Sri Lanka take the time out and visit this amazing place Adams Peak. A scenic train trip from Kandy, followed by a drive though hill country, visit a tea factory and stay in Dalhousie, enjoy the surrounding splendour before the climb.  Consider a sunset climb less crowds. Join the pilgrimage of people, it’s so pleasing and you can draw on each other for strength even when you’re hurting a little.  I walked along-side a couple of monks trekking up barefoot very inspiring stuff. Travelled in February 2015.

I climbed Sri pada(Adam's peak) with my wife and three daughters in mid-April this year. Because I have been to Sri Pada once before, I knew it is going to be difficult for the little ones and planned everything well ahead.We checked into a close by guest house during the early afternoon and slept for six hours. We wanted to be at the top to watch the sunrise. People usually start climbing at about 2 am. But, we started the 5500 step hike at about 10 pm the previous night. Night time is better than climbing during day time as it is cooler at night. The girls enjoyed the first mile or so chanting "they can do it " breaking the night's silence.However, I ran into problems when they started feeling sleepy and tired. I had to carry them at some places when they refused to move. The kids enjoyed the exercise of tying a string to a miniature walking stick and taking the thread up along the side of the road creating a web of threads.This is at 'Indikatupana' midway in the hike. The last bit with steep steps('Mahagiridamba') was really challenging because the girls were exhausted and started crying. When we finally reached the temple at the summit, it is 6.30 am(8 and a half hours walk !) and there was no sunrise seen because it was a cloudy day. The tired little pilgrims went to sleep in the rest room- an open space with a roof. I felt helpless as I wasn't prepared for this. We had to protect them from chilling winds by covering them with one blanket and our jackets. We stayed at the top for about four hours before we started to set down. Though it was relatively easy, the kids sweared that they will never ever visit Sri Pada again..a family hike turned into a painful experience. If someone plans to hike up with kids, a few tips that might help... 1. Travel light- don't bring water- there are shops that sell mineral water bottles until you are 500 yards from the top.Though they cost a little bit more you will appreciate a lighter backpack when you are nearing the top. 2. Pack ponchos - the weather is unpredictable and can rain during the season unexpectedly 3. Don't climb straight away after a long drive. There are plenty of good quality guest houses at the foot step of the mountain 5-10 minutes walk from the entrance.
